messages:
incident-bot: Pager: Increased generation latency detected for model-gen-us-west. P50 > 1s, P99 > 10s. Triggered by latency detector rule gen_latency_us_west.
Alice (oncall): seeing it, thanks. digging into routing and queues now.
Alice (oncall): @Ben I'm going to page you for handoff in 10m if this doesn't stabilize.
Priya (sre-lead): @Alice quick note — check recent deploys in us-west and any autoscaling events. I've seen similar from a bad kernel on nvidia node pool last month.
Alice (oncall): pulling logs. running `kubectl logs -n inference svc-gen-usw -c runtime --since=10m | tail -n 200`
Mateo (prod-comms): heads up, I'll start drafting an internal status blurb once we know customer impact. Keep me posted.
Alice (oncall): initial findings: continuous batching queue depth spiking, KV cache misses increasing, 5XXs not elevated yet but tail latency is bad. suspect degraded GPU host performance.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-345 - High generation latency (us-west). Severity: P1. Pager routed to oncall.
Emily (support): do we have any customer reports? I see 2 tickets about slow responses in the dashboard. tagging @Mateo.
Ben (next-oncall): joining. @Alice handover? what's current mitigation?
Alice (oncall): hey @Ben -- timeline: 00:00 detector fires, queues up, autoscaler attempted 2x scale but nodes didn't join. Possible kubelet crash on a subset of hosts. Mitigations attempted: evict pods on a few nodes, restarted runtime process on one replica — partial recovery for one shard.
Ben (next-oncall): ok, I'll take over in 5. Can you paste the status page copy you want? I can publish once comms review approves.
Mateo (prod-comms): draft for status page (initial):
```
We are investigating increased generation latency affecting requests in the us-west region. Some requests may experience slow or delayed responses. Our engineering team is actively working on mitigation. We will provide updates every 15 minutes.```
Mateo (prod-comms): pinging @Priya and @Alice for technical accuracy.
Priya (sre-lead): accurate. Add note: ``No evidence of data loss or incorrect outputs. Requests may time out or be delayed.``
Alice (oncall): adding operational note: `Affected service: svc-gen-usw; mitigation in progress: cordon problematic nodes and redistribute shards.`
Mateo (prod-comms): OK I have a short version for the public status page and an expanded internal note for support. I'm ready to publish initial update if @Priya and oncall ok.
Priya (sre-lead): approve initial text. @statuspage-bot publish draft?
statuspage-bot: Draft published to status.redwood.ai - Incident: Increased generation latency in us-west (initial). Scheduled for public posting after QA.
Alice (oncall): continuing mitigation: cordoned 4 nodes, recreated pods, KV cache warming in progress. P50 down to 400ms, P99 still ~3s.
Emily (support): I've posted the internal support note to the ticket queue and added the public draft link. Customers on the 1:1 escalations notified.
Mateo (prod-comms): publishing initial public update now.
statuspage-bot: Public update posted: "We're investigating increased generation latency in the us-west region. No data loss is suspected. Engineers are working on mitigation." Update ID: UPD-2313456789-1
Ben (next-oncall): taking over full oncall. Alice, handing off logs and command history. I'll own the rest of the mitigations.
Alice (oncall): handing off monitoring dashboards and the `kubectl` session output. Good luck, Ben.
Ben (next-oncall): thanks — immediate next steps: continue node reboot/replace cycle, increase traffic fallthrough to eu region for new requests, add rate limit safeguards for heavy prefixes.
Priya (sre-lead): agree. Also enable temporary fallback routing (route-policy: cost-aware -> latency-priority) so new requests prefer eu/central while we stabilize us-west.
incident-bot: Scheduled update reminder: next status update due in 15 minutes.
Mateo (prod-comms): draft for periodic update (15m):
```
Engineering has made progress: partial recovery observed after node replacements and pod restarts. P50 latency improved; some requests still see delays. We continue to route traffic away from affected hosts and expect further improvements. No customer data loss. Next update in 30 minutes or sooner.
```
Mateo (prod-comms): tagging @Emily for support copy.
Emily (support): got it, updating ticket macros.
Ben (next-oncall): follow-up: after additional node replacements, P99 down to 800ms. Steady improvement. I'll keep routing fallback for 30m then reassess.
statuspage-bot: Public update posted: UPD-2313456789-2 - Partial recovery observed; routing changes applied.
Mateo (prod-comms): good. I'll prepare resolved copy when Ben confirms stable for 1h.
Ben (next-oncall): confirming stable for 45m with P99 < 900ms and error rates normal. No new customer escalations.
Priya (sre-lead): recommend monitoring for another 30m then mark resolved.
Ben (next-oncall): agreed. Moving to monitor-only.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-345 moved to monitoring.
Mateo (prod-comms): resolved status page draft:
```
Resolved: The generation latency issue in the us-west region has been resolved. The root cause was a subset of GPU hosts experiencing kernel-level instability which prevented new nodes from joining the cluster. Engineering replaced affected hosts and redistributed shards; latency and error rates have returned to normal. No customer data loss was observed. If you continue to see issues, please contact support.
```
statuspage-bot: Final update posted and incident marked resolved. Final Update ID: UPD-2313456789-3
Emily (support): I notified customers in escalations and updated ticket macros with resolved notice.
Alice (oncall): thanks everyone. Will follow up with a postmortem draft tomorrow covering root cause, remediation, and permanent mitigations.
Priya (sre-lead): thanks all. Assigning postmortem owners: @Alice (lead) + @Ben (ops follow-up).
Mateo (prod-comms): closing comms loop; I'll post the final status page link in the incident doc and send the public-facing note to the outreach list. :thumbsup:
Ben (next-oncall): handing off to next rotation.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-345 closed at 2313457689.
